en: The Ifugao people use the muyong woodlot system to prevent landslides and ensure a clean water supply for their rice terraces.
During the Pahiyas Festival, locals use natural kiping made from rice dough instead of plastic to create safe, biodegradable decorations.
The Philippine national flower, Sampaguita, is used in traditional medicine to relieve fever and headaches when its leaves are brewed as tea.
The Magna Carta of Public Health Workers guarantees Filipino health professionals safe working conditions and adequate protective equipment during disease outbreaks.
National Scientist Dr. Fe del Mundo invented a bamboo incubator to keep newborns warm in rural areas without electricity.
The Filipino value of bayanihan involves neighbors physically helping each other move entire nipa huts to safer locations during floods.
T'boli weavers use natural plant dyes and beeswax for T'nalak cloth, avoiding toxic synthetic chemicals that can cause severe skin allergies.
The DepEd Oplan Balik Eskwela program requires schools to inspect buildings for structural safety and fire hazards before classes begin.
Traditional hilot massage uses coconut oil to reduce skin friction and prevent muscle tears during physical therapy and relaxation.
Filipino sailors historically used fermented bagoong to safely preserve protein through lactic acid fermentation during long sea voyages.
National Artist Guillermo Tolentino used structurally sound bronze casting to ensure his Oblation statue safely withstands outdoor weathering and corrosion.
The Ecological Solid Waste Management Act requires every barangay to maintain a Materials Recovery Facility to safely segregate recyclable trash.
